question: Does a single-domain particle with uniaxial anisotropy keep one of two magnetization directions, and how does the direction of the applied field change the way one is written?

provenance.source: E. C. Stoner and E. P. Wohlfarth, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 240, 599 (1948)

name: Stoner-Wohlfarth particle

carrier.name: magnetization angle, measured from the hard axis

closure: single domain (exchange keeps the magnetization uniform); overdamped Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert relaxation in the plane that contains the easy axis and the field; thermal bath
observable: magnetization along the easy axis, sin(phi) (magnetometry or the magneto-optical Kerr effect)
assumptions: energy per volume in units of 2K: e = cos(phi)^2 / 2 - h cos(phi - phi_field), with phi measured from the hard axis, so that the easy axis is phi = +-pi/2
reduced field h = mu0 Ms H / (2K); psi is the angle between the field and the easy axis, and the field points along phi_field = pi/2 - psi
overdamped (large Gilbert damping) motion confined to the plane of the easy axis and the field; the precession out of the plane is not modelled
time in units of the relaxation time (1 + alpha^2) Ms / (2 gamma K alpha)
noise D = kT / (2KV) = 0.05 chosen for the example; particles used for data storage have D of about 0.01
